description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is transaction.TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent artefacts say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 '* Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224 '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', whose neighbour at README.md:223 gives 'Transaction View' to CT01/COTRN01C - the exact inverse of the prompt's mapping, and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Both line numbers were verified in this checkout rather than copied: README.md is unmodified since the initial commit, :222 is the CT00/'Transaction List' row, and the CT02 row is :224. Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected. Nothing in this case is downgraded to read-only to match the name: the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20, and this case stops one step short of it on purpose. WHAT THIS CASE PINS - THE TOLERATED SEVERITY-3 DATE, AND THE CONFIRM PROMPT IT REACHES: both CSUTLDTC call sites are exercised in one run, and they return DIFFERENT outcomes. Site 1 at :389-407 validates TORIGDTI '2022-07-18' and gets severity '0000' with message number '0000', so :397-398 CONTINUE. Site 2 at :409-427 validates TPROCDTI '1500-01-01' and gets severity '0003' with message number '2513', so :417 fails, :420's inner IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM NOT = '2513' is FALSE, and NOTHING HAPPENS - no message, no error flag, no cursor move, no send. Validation continues to :430-436, MIDI '123456789' IS NUMERIC, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS completes with WS-ERR-FLG still 'N' and WS-MESSAGE still SPACES, and control returns to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY :169. CONFIRMI is a single blank, so the EVALUATE takes its SPACES arm at :175-181: 'Y' to WS-ERR-FLG, 'Confirm to add this transaction...' to WS-MESSAGE, -1 to CONFIRML, and PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN. That is the whole observable outcome: one send, one message, no write. THE ACCEPTANCE RULE IS A TWO-LEVEL NESTED IF WITH THREE OUTCOMES, AND THIS CASE DRIVES TWO OF THEM. Verbatim at :397-407 and again at :417-427: IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD = '0000' CONTINUE ELSE IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM NOT = '2513' then rejects, END-IF END-IF. Branch A is severity '0000' - accepted outright by the explicit CONTINUE. Branch B is a NON-'0000' severity whose message number IS '2513' - the inner condition is false, the END-IF is reached with no statement executed, and the date is TOLERATED. Branch C is a non-'0000' severity whose message number is anything else - rejected with its own literal and its own cursor field. This case drives branch A at site 1 and branch B at site 2, which is both acceptance branches in one file; case17 drives branch C at site 1 with TORIGDTI '2022-13-01' (FC-INVALID-MONTH, 2517) and its 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' message on TORIGDTL. Branch B has no message and no cursor of its own, so the only way to observe it is exactly this: reach a LATER outcome that a rejection would have made unreachable, because SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends the task. PRACTICE B5 - THE RULING FOR THIS FILE, STATED PLAINLY. The source GRANTS an exemption to exactly one error value, and this case preserves it exactly as granted. '2513' is FC-UNSUPP-RANGE, declared at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:66 as 88 FC-UNSUPP-RANGE VALUE X'000309D159C3C5C5'; the first halfword X'0003' is SEVERITY PIC S9(4) BINARY = 3 and the second X'09D1' is MSG-NO PIC S9(4) BINARY = 9*256 + 209 = 2513, and :137-138 gives it the 15-character result text 'Unsupp. Range  '. It means the date lies outside the range CEEDAYS supports - before the Lillian epoch of 15 October 1582 - and the legacy programs deliberately let those through. That this is intentional rather than an oversight is evidenced by CORPT00C, which grants the IDENTICAL exemption at both of its own call sites (app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl:396-407 for the start date and :416-427 for the end date): four call sites in two programs, all four spelling the same NOT = '2513'. Therefore: do NOT treat all severity-3 outcomes as rejections; do NOT harden the check by dropping the '2513' exemption; do NOT rationalise it away as a bug to be fixed. Hardening it would refuse dates the legacy program accepts, which is a changed business rule and a parity failure, and it would do so silently because no message marks the tolerated path. THE NINE FEEDBACK TOKENS, EVERY HEX VALUE DECODED HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED (app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:62-70, first halfword SEVERITY, second halfword MSG-NO): FC-INVALID-DATE X'0000000000000000' = severity 0, message 0, 'Date is valid'; FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA X'000309CB59C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09CB' 2507, 'Insufficient'; FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE X'000309CC59C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09CC' 2508, 'Datevalue error'; FC-INVALID-ERA X'000309CD59C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09CD' 2509, 'Invalid Era    '; FC-UNSUPP-RANGE X'000309D159C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09D1' 2513, 'Unsupp. Range  ' - THE TOLERATED ONE; FC-INVALID-MONTH X'000309D559C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09D5' 2517, 'Invalid month  '; FC-BAD-PIC-STRING X'000309D659C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09D6' 2518, 'Bad Pic String '; FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA X'000309D859C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09D8' 2520, 'Nonnumeric data'; FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO X'000309D959C3C5C5' = 3 / X'09D9' 2521, 'YearInEra is 0 '; and an unmatched token falls to WHEN OTHER at :147-148 with 'Date is invalid'. Ten arms, ordered, WHEN OTHER last (gate G30, rule R7). Only ONE of those nine numbers is exempt at the call sites, and 2513 is it. PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED, NEVER CAPTURED (practice B12, risk R-A). Every value here comes from reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl and app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl and from decoding the 88-level hex VALUEs above by hand; none of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, because no COBOL runs in this environment. Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, and the one that bites here is decisive: cobc --list-intrinsics matches ZERO CEE* entries, so CEEDAYS - the routine CSUTLDTC:116 calls and whose feedback code is the entire subject of this case - cannot be executed at all. The Java side is nevertheless verified rather than asserted: util.DateUtilityJob is a hand-written CEEDAYS equivalent, deterministic and with no clock or locale input, so the two outcomes this case needs are produced by two date literals instead of by a mock, and the harness reaches the real service. GATE G12 - CSUTLDTC IS A SPRING @Service, NOT A JOB. No EXEC PGM= names CSUTLDTC anywhere in app/jcl/, app/proc/ or app/csd/; it is a called subprogram, reached from four sites in two ONLINE programs (CORPT00C :392 and :412, COTRN02C :393 and :413). Its prompt-mandated Java name is util.DateUtilityJob, and rule R1 keeps that name verbatim, but implicit requirement I3 fixes what it IS: a @Service, constructor-injected into transaction.TransactionViewController and called as a plain method - never a Spring Batch Job, Step or Tasklet, and never launched. There are no jobParameters on this case for the same reason, and the unit kind is CONTROLLER_POJO: the controller is constructed and its handler invoked directly, with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). THE TWO OUTCOMES ARE ORDERED, AND THE ORDERING IS THE POINT. A translation that satisfied both calls with one value could not distinguish accept from tolerate, so the two literals differ and each is pinned to its own site: site 1 receives TORIGDTI '2022-07-18' and must yield severity '0000' / message '0000' / 'Date is valid  ' / RETURN-CODE 0; site 2 receives TPROCDTI '1500-01-01' and must yield severity '0003' / message '2513' / 'Unsupp. Range  ' / RETURN-CODE 3. Both literals are pinned rather than computed (practice B7), and '1500-01-01' is the same literal COTRN02CParityTest names TOLERATED_DATE so the case file and the direct assertions describe one concept with one value. The boundary date '1582-10-14' - Lillian day 0, the day immediately before the epoch - yields the same token and the same 2513, while '1582-10-15' is Lillian day 1 and reports '0000'; the tolerance therefore has a real edge and this case sits well inside it. THE 80-BYTE CSUTLDTC-RESULT, SUMMED TWICE (practice B11). The caller's own view at app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:62-69 is CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD PIC X(04) at 1-4, FILLER PIC X(11) at 5-15, CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM PIC X(04) at 16-19 and CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG PIC X(61) at 20-80: 4 + 11 + 4 + 61 = 80. The producer's WS-MESSAGE at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:42-57 is byte-aligned with it: WS-SEVERITY X(04) 1-4 (WS-SEVERITY-N REDEFINES it as 9(4)), FILLER X(11) VALUE 'Mesg Code:' 5-15 which is ten characters and one trailing space, WS-MSG-NO X(04) 16-19 (WS-MSG-NO-N REDEFINES as 9(4)), FILLER X(01) SPACE 20, WS-RESULT X(15) 21-35, FILLER X(01) SPACE 36, FILLER X(09) VALUE 'TstDate:' 37-45, WS-DATE X(10) 46-55, FILLER X(01) SPACE 56, FILLER X(10) VALUE 'Mask used:' 57-66, WS-DATE-FMT X(10) 67-76, FILLER X(01) SPACE 77 and FILLER X(03) SPACES 78-80: 4 + 11 + 4 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 9 + 10 + 1 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 3 = 80. Both sums are 80 and the two views agree at every offset, which is why a caller can read the severity and the message number out of the middle of someone else's message text at all. THE TWO RETURNED IMAGES IN FULL, EVEN THOUGH ONLY EIGHT BYTES ARE READ (practice B8). Site 1 returns, in US-ASCII, "0000Mesg Code: 0000 Date is valid   TstDate: " then X'00' X'0A' then "2022-07- Mask used:YYYY-MM-DD" then four spaces; site 2 returns "0003Mesg Code: 2513 Unsupp. Range   TstDate: " then X'00' X'0A' then "1500-01- Mask used:YYYY-MM-DD" then four spaces. Each is exactly 80 bytes. COTRN02C reads only bytes 1-4 and 16-19 of them, and the remaining 72 bytes are never inspected by this program - they are recorded here so that a reviewer can check the offsets rather than trust them. Two source quirks are visible and both are preserved (practice B5): INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at CSUTLDTC:90 does not clear FILLER items, so 'Mesg Code:', 'TstDate:' and 'Mask used:' survive into every result; and the GROUP move MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE at CSUTLDTC:122 copies the two-byte BINARY VSTRING-LENGTH halfword - X'000A', decimal 10 - in front of the text, so WS-DATE X(10) at bytes 46-55 holds those two bytes plus only the first EIGHT characters of the date and the day digits fall off the right. Bytes 46 and 47 are therefore not character data. The definitive treatment of that quirk belongs to parity/CSUTLDTC, which owns CSUTLDTC's own twenty cases; it is derived here from app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl directly rather than depended upon. CSUTLDTC'S RETURN-CODE 3 DOES NOT BECOME COTRN02C'S, SO expectedReturnCode IS 0 AND NOT 3. CSUTLDTC:98 does MOVE WS-SEVERITY-N TO RETURN-CODE, so the subprogram really does return 3 for every named error including FC-UNSUPP-RANGE. COTRN02C never reads RETURN-CODE, never tests it and contains ZERO occurrences of CALL 'CEE3ABD' - verified by counting them in the source - so there is no path from a severity-3 date to a non-zero exit here. That matters most on precisely this case: a severity-3 result is ACCEPTED, and the outcome must be an ordinary continuation rather than a failure of any kind. Gate G35 is therefore NOT applicable to this program and is not asserted; neither is G32, since COTRN02C contains zero GO TO statements (rule R7). THE CONFIRM EVALUATE AT :169-188, ARM SHARING INTACT (gate G30). 'Y' at :170 and 'y' at :171 SHARE one block, PERFORM ADD-TRANSACTION at :172. 'N' at :173, 'n' at :174, SPACES at :175 and LOW-VALUES at :176 SHARE one block at :177-181 - 'Y' to WS-ERR-FLG, 'Confirm to add this transaction...' to WS-MESSAGE, -1 to CONFIRML, PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN. WHEN OTHER at :182 takes :183-187, identical in shape but carrying 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' instead, also with -1 to CONFIRML. A translation that split either shared block, or that reordered the arms, or that put WHEN OTHER anywhere but last, would be a different program. This case owns the SPACES arm. The 'Y' and 'y' arms are owned by case19, which writes the 350-byte record and reports 'Transaction added successfully.  Your Tran ID is ...', and by case20, which hits the duplicate-key path; the WHEN OTHER arm yields the byte-exact 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' with -1 to CONFIRML and is documented here rather than given a file of its own, because gate G15 fixes this folder at twenty cases - case01 through case20 - and no case21.json may exist. THE POSITIONAL GUARD AND THE SEMANTIC CHECK ARE TWO SEPARATE LAYERS, AND THIS CASE'S DATES PASS BOTH. The first layer is textual and knows nothing about calendars: :353-366 for TORIGDTI and :368-381 for TPROCDTI test (1:4) IS NUMERIC, (5:1) EQUAL '-', (6:2) NUMERIC, (8:1) EQUAL '-' and (9:2) NUMERIC - a 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10 decomposition of the X(10) field - and on failure report 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' or 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD'. The second layer is the CSUTLDTC call, which asks whether the date EXISTS. '1500-01-01' passes the first layer completely - four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits - and is a perfectly real date; it fails only the third question, whether Language Environment supports it, and that failure is the one the caller forgives. Conflating the two layers would lose exactly this case: a well-formed, real, unsupported date that the program accepts. HOW THE RUN REACHES THE DATE CHECKS AT ALL. EIBCALEN is 218, so :115's zero guard is not taken and :119 moves the whole area into CARDDEMO-COMMAREA; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true, :120's NOT test fails, and :132 performs RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN before :133's EVALUATE EIBAID matches DFHENTER at :134 and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY (gate G38 - this is the REENTER half). VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS takes its first arm at :196 because ACTIDINI is '00000000050' rather than spaces; :197's IS NOT NUMERIC test fails on eleven digits; :204 computes WS-ACCT-ID-N with FUNCTION NUMVAL; :206-207 moves it to XREF-ACCT-ID and back into ACTIDINI as eleven zero-padded digits; :208 performs READ-CXACAIX-FILE, whose EXEC CICS READ at :578-586 returns DFHRESP(NORMAL) and takes the CONTINUE arm at :589-590 (gate G47); and :209 moves XREF-CARD-NUM into CARDNINI, which is how CARDNINO comes back as '0500024453765740' from an input of sixteen blanks. VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS then finds WS-ERR-FLG off, so :237's blanking of the eleven detail fields is skipped; the eleven emptiness arms at :252-317 all miss and fall to WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :318-319; TTYPCDI '01' and TCATCDI '0001' are numeric so :322-337 falls to its own WHEN OTHER; and the amount shape guard at :339-351 passes on '+00000012.34' - (1:1) is '+', (2:8) '00000012' is numeric, (10:1) is '.' and (11:2) '34' is numeric. THE AMOUNT IS RE-EDITED BEFORE EITHER DATE IS CHECKED, AND THE RE-EDITED FORM IS WHAT THIS CASE ASSERTS. :383-386 runs first: COMPUTE WS-TRAN-AMT-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(TRNAMTI) into PIC S9(9)V99, MOVE WS-TRAN-AMT-N TO WS-TRAN-AMT-E which is PIC +99999999.99, then MOVE WS-TRAN-AMT-E back into TRNAMTI. '+00000012.34' is already in the canonical edited form, so it round-trips to itself - which is the assertion: the value on the screen afterwards is the OUTPUT of the edit, not the input that happened to look like it, and case15 pins the same edit changing its input. The numeric policy is BigDecimal at scale exactly 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN through common.CobolDecimal (rules R2, R3 and R4; gates G23 and G24), because the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO times in all 28 programs and COBOL therefore truncates on store; never double, never float, never HALF_UP and never HALF_EVEN. WHAT THE EXPECTATION SAYS, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. expectedMessages carries exactly ONE message, on its two channels: WS_MESSAGE_80 holds 'Confirm to add this transaction...' - 34 characters - left-justified and space-padded to the 80 bytes WS-MESSAGE is declared at :38, and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 holds the same text padded to the 78 bytes ERRMSGO is declared at in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY:144, which is the two-byte loss of MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :520 (rule R5). There is deliberately NO 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' anywhere in this expectation: that literal is what branch C would have produced, and its absence is the assertion. CONFIRML is -1 and is the ONLY length item this case sets: a length item is validation metadata taken from the symbolic map's COMP PIC S9(4) 'L' items and never a JSON payload member, so it appears as cursorField 'CONFIRML' and nowhere else. TORIGDTO and TPROCDTO come back UNCHANGED at '2022-07-18' and '1500-01-01' - the acceptance path rewrites neither, and a translation that normalised the unsupported date would be caught here. The six header fields come from POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 with the clock pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, giving CURDATEO '07/19/22' from WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' from WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS (practice B7). ERRMSGC is DFHDFCOL because COTRN02C's ONLY attribute assignment is MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :727 on the successful-write arm, which this path never reaches. NOTHING IS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS PINNED THREE WAYS. The confirm prompt short-circuits before ADD-TRANSACTION, so there is no EXEC CICS STARTBR at :645, no READPREV at :676 and no WRITE at :713: expectedWrites is empty, expectedFinalState pins all three seeded TRANSACT rows byte for byte and unchanged, and expectedDatasets pins TRANSACT on the FINAL_STATE channel at three rows of 350 bytes each - the width CVTRA05Y declares, FILLER included (gate G21). termination is RETURN_TRANSID because SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends at :530-534 with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), not with an XCTL, and nextProgram is COTRN02C itself with nextMapset COTRN02 and nextMap COTRN2A from the SEND at :522-528. No XCTL happens on this path, so gate G40 has no subject here. All 22 fields of the 218-byte area are pinned and none omitted, because the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in server-side session state (rule R6, gates G37 and G38) and an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked. The area is 218 bytes because COCOM01Y is 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 = 160 and the CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at :72-80 is 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58; the extension stays a separate DTO field and is never folded into the 160-byte NavigationContext. The sent map is 555 bytes - 12 leading FILLER plus 21 fields at 7 bytes of metadata each plus 396 bytes of payload - and all 21 payload items are pinned at their declared widths (practice B11). THE SEEDED DATASETS, ADDRESSED BY BINDING KEY ONLY (gate G46). CCXREF is seeded from fixtures/cardxref.txt, five rows from row zero, and row zero is the one that matters: XREF-CARD-NUM '0500024453765740' at bytes 1-16, XREF-CUST-ID '000000050' at 17-25 and XREF-ACCT-ID '00000000050' at 26-36. It is seeded RAW at 36 bytes and is NOT pre-padded here: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = 50 and the fixture supplies only 36, omitting the trailing FILLER X(14), and ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow is the declared sole owner of that 36-to-50 pad, requested through the single CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation (gate G16, risk R-F). There is deliberately NO separate CXACAIX seed: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-65 defines CXACAIX as DSNAME ...CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH with DESCRIPTION 'ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY', so it is a PATH over the CCXREF base and is reached as an alternate-index FINDER on one repository rather than as a second dataset (gate G45). TRANSACT is seeded inline with three 350-byte rows so that 'nothing was written' is provable against a non-empty master rather than merely against an absent one. No tenth fixture is introduced - the set is closed at the nine files of app/data/ASCII - and no dataset anywhere here is addressed by a fully-qualified mainframe dataset name. The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND IS PRESERVED AS ONE (practice B5). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE at :40 is declared PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' and appears in NO DATASET operand anywhere in the program - the only six DATASET operands are WS-CXACAIX-FILE at :579, WS-CCXREF-FILE at :612 and WS-TRANSACT-FILE at :645, :676, :705 and :714 - and COPY CVACT01Y at :89 brings in the 300-byte ACCOUNT-RECORD that nothing then reads or writes. It is seeded here so the deadness is visible rather than invisible, and it is the reason no ACCTDAT row appears in expectedWrites or expectedFinalState in this case or in any other case in this folder. Removing the declaration, or wiring it up to make it look used, would both be changes to a program this migration is forbidden to change. GOVERNING PRACTICES. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that line is the whole document - confirmed twice for this file. No user rule governs it, and their absence is not licence to lower the bar: Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 binds instead, and the practices that decide this file are B5 above all - the '2513' tolerance is preserved exactly as the source grants it - together with B4 on disclosing rather than correcting the R-B inversion, B12 on honest static-derivation provenance including the unavailability of CEEDAYS, B8 on being explicit about both outcomes, both 80-byte images, the exact message text, the -1 target, the scale and rounding mode, the binding keys and the code page, B7 on pinning the clock and both date literals to fixed values rather than computing a today, B1 on shipping no unfilled value and computing every hex decode, B11 on summing 80 twice and decomposing 10, 218, 555 and 396 in the open, and B3 on treating app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/jcl, app/proc, app/csd, app/ctl, app/catlg and app/data as read-only. Rules R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 bind as cited above. Gates in play: G12, G15, G16, G18, G23, G24, G30, G37, G38, G45, G46, G47 and G51. Gates deliberately not asserted because this program has no subject for them: G32, G35, G39, G40 and G43, and G36 belongs to parity/CSUTLDTC.
